notes.title: Small Game Update: v0.0.6-alpha and Test Build Release on Itch.io
notes.notes:
[h3]Greetings Counselor,[/h3][p][/p][p]Since our last update, a lot has been happening behind the scenes. While most of our work has focused on mechanics, systems, and the game's campaign that go beyond this test build, we would also like to give more players a chance to experience the game early. Therefore starting today, the test build is now available on [url="https://loge-games.itch.io/jury-trial"]Itch.io[/url] as well.[/p][p]Players can now choose to download the test build directly from Itch.io or continue playing through Steam by requesting a key via [url="https://discord.com/invite/bQNesxtakY"]our Discord[/url]. In our previous post, we mentioned that the test build would be coming to an end, but given the steady flow of new players interested in trying it out, we’ve decided to keep it available for now.[/p][p]With the Itch.io release, we’ve also updated the test build with some quality-of-life changes and a few new select mechanics. As mentioned before, most of our recent work has been under the hood and is therefore not visible in the test build. But one example worth noting, even though it isn’t available yet, is our work on the Case Editor. Since the campaign is being built in the same editor that players will have access to at launch, we’ve taken every opportunity to smooth out hurdles and improve workflow during the campaign’s case creation. Because of this, the Case Editor has really grown over the past few weeks and is looking better and better.[/p][p]This means the number of changes is smaller compared to past updates where we overhauled or expanded systems, but you’ll still find some meaningful additions. The most notable change for returning players will be that players can now use Jury Actions to uncover hidden juror traits before jury selection, alongside a few other refinements aimed at smoother gameplay. And while the case’s story remains unchanged, these additions give both new and returning players fresh ways to approach the process of selecting the right jurors for the case.[/p][p]So without further ado, here’s what’s new in version 0.0.6 - alpha:[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Change Log[/b]
[i](Note: this list covers player-facing features and excludes under-the-hood changes made in recent weeks.)[/i][/p][list][*][p]Added new music tracks for the dossier and courtroom scenes.[/p][/*][*][p]Added facial expressions to dialog creation. Case Creators can now assign character expressions to their lines.[/p][/*][*][p]Enabled Jury Actions (document search, relationship search, internet search, court psychiatrist). These allow players to reveal hidden juror traits before selection. Each action targets specific trait groups with higher discovery chances based on its field. Case Creators can set the number of uses and how many attributes are revealed per action.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a search filter to the evidence page for quicker text-based filtering.[/p][/*][*][p]Enabled the plaintiff polaroid in the dossier’s person tab. It now displays information about the plaintiff (the state in this case), configurable by Case Creators.[/p][/*][*][p]Revamped Judge Strike, Juror/Witness Strike, and Breakdown mechanics so they now function independently.[/p][/*][*][p]Renamed Opening Arguments to Opening Statements for proper terminology.[/p][/*][*][p]Transcripts are no longer split when using the recess option. They now remain as a single continuous log.[/p][/*][*][p]Characters capable of striking out the player or breaking down now have unique dialogue lines defined by Case Creators.[/p][/*][*][p]Added tooltips to witnesses in court to show their traits.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed various inconsistencies and issues, added new sprites, and improved overall polish.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][p]That’s everything for this round. As always, thank you for testing, providing feedback, and helping us shape the game![/p][p]Cheers,[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39390578/4e49a56d89604c53cbc6b035af1e3ac7e769d269.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Game Update: v0.0.5-alpha Change Log
notes.notes:
[b]Greetings Counsel,[/b]

Today, alpha version 0.0.5 has been released. While the changes in this build may seem minor, their impact on the game is quite significant. Since the last update, we have been working on the save system, and we’re happy to announce that it is now possible to save the game during a court session or meeting.

The new ‘Recess’ option in the HUD allows you to request a quick break during court days or meetings. When the timing is appropriate and the judge grants permission, the recess feature takes you back to the case folder. Here, you can review materials if needed, but more importantly, you can now save and load the game mid-scene.

This ensures that you can save, load, exit, and resume the game at any time without worrying about losing progress. Implementing this feature required extensive modifications to multiple scenes and systems, but we believe it was time well spent.


[i]New Feature[/i]
It is now possible to save and load the game during the following scenes:
[list]
[*] Meetings
[*]Opening and closing arguments
[*]Witness questioning
[/list]
[i]Improvements and Fixes[/i]
[list]
[*]The defendant now rises when the judge announces the sentencing
[*]Text that was too long for speech bubbles or the dialogue GUI has been resized to fit properly
[*]Fixed an issue where a person could be scheduled for court despite being dismissed or missing
[*]Added an info tooltip for witnesses
[*]Various other minor issues have been corrected
[/list]
Thank you for your continued support! If you have feedback or encounter any issues with the new build, please let us know on [url=https://discord.com/invite/bQNesxtakY]Discord[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39390578/4e49a56d89604c53cbc6b035af1e3ac7e769d269.png[/img]

notes.title: Game Update: v0.0.3-alpha Change Log
notes.notes:
Greetings, Counselor,

Today, alpha build 0.0.3 has been released! Besides some quality-of-life improvements and smaller adjustments, this update mainly focuses on changes to the jury questioning process and the introduction of an automatic transcript feature.

[i]Improvements and Fixes[/i]

[i]Jury Questioning[/i]
[list]
[*] Jury questioning is no longer limited to four mandatory days where the player must question five potential jurors each day.
[*]Players can now schedule the questioning of jurors in the same manner as scheduling a meeting.
[*]This gives players complete freedom to decide when and how many potential jurors they wish to question.
[*] A questioning session can be scheduled anytime between the Pre-Trial Conference and the Jury Selection date.
[*]If the player schedules more than one potential juror for a single day, they will return to the case folder after each questioning session, allowing them to save in between.
[*]To accommodate the new system, the jury questioning assessment has been removed, and an overview of the selected jury has been added, which is shown after completing the selection.
[/list]
[i]Further Changes[/i]
[list]
[*] An automatic transcript feature has been introduced, enabling players to re-read dialogue from past meetings, court days, and the current scene. This is accessible within the case folder and during a scene.
[*]The Jury Pool tab within the case folder has been reworked for better usability and clarity.
[*]The dialog GUI now highlights which dialogue options have already been used and indicates if any unused dialogue remains within a topic or piece of evidence. When all available dialogue has been exhausted, the entry point automatically grays out and becomes unclickable. If new dialogue becomes available, the entry point reactivates, making it easy to spot and engage with the updated content.
[*]The rating GUI for jurors, which helps players take notes during the questioning process, is now accessible through the juror sheet button. It has been replaced by a better overview of known and unknown traits, along with a note about the juror.
[*]In this note, Case Creators can provide players with hints or other useful information, similar to the assessments on the person page. This note can also be accessed during juror questioning and selection within the rating GUI.
[*]The Legal Situation tab has been slightly adjusted to improve the display of compulsory and supporting arguments.
[*]Multiple typographical errors and other minor issues have been corrected.
[/list]
Thank you for your ongoing support!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39390578/4e49a56d89604c53cbc6b035af1e3ac7e769d269.png[/img]

notes.title: Game Update: v0.0.2-alpha Change Log
notes.notes:
Greetings Counsel,

Based on the feedback from the current test, we've released a small update that includes fixes, improvements, and several requested features. Please note that not all changes will apply to your existing save game and may require starting a new game.

[i]New Features:[/i]

[list]
[*] Added an indicator on the Office Tab to highlight unread messages in the inbox.
[*] Unread messages in the inbox now appear in bold until they are read.
[*] Players can now skip the juror walk-in sequence during trial days (opening statements, closing arguments, witness hearings, and verdict).
[*] Tooltips have been updated to display the person's name, role, and all associated traits.
[*] The defendant is now included in Jury Selection, making it easier to review their traits.
[*] A save confirmation prompt has been added to prevent accidental saving due to misclicks.
[/list]

[i]Improvements and Fixes:[/i]

[list]
[*] Increased the likelihood that a juror will reveal a trait hint during jury questioning.
[*] The first client meeting is now scheduled with a fixed date rather than through the event system. [i]Note: Previously, if the player scheduled the meeting manually before the event system triggered on day one after the case started, the incarceration event could become misaligned.[/i]
[*] The Jury Pool Religion filter now correctly filters for the religion of Thule.
[*] Strikeout texts for jurors and judges are now correctly displayed.
[*] The number of strike points for the judge has been increased.
[*] Increased spacing between dialogue options in the dialogue GUI for better usability on smaller screens.
[*] The game is now properly centered on widescreen resolutions.
[*] Fixed a bug that caused evidence material descriptions to disappear after cycling and switching materials.
[*] Players can now scroll through objection options in the objection GUI using the mouse wheel.
[*] The tutorial has been slightly updated and now includes a link to upcoming changes in the Jury Questioning system.
[*] A few misplaced strikes on answers during jury questioning have been removed.
[*] Multiple typographical errors and other minor issues have been corrected
[/list]

We appreciate your continued support and if you missed the upcoming changes to the Jury Questioning process, you can find them [url=https://discord.com/channels/740945268337541152/1257155112925659179/1286104269518540872]here[/url].

notes.title: Development Update - The Jury Questioning
notes.notes:
Greetings Counselors,

It has been a while since our last update, and if you haven't joined our [url=https://discord.com/invite/bQNesxtakY]Discord[/url] server yet, you're probably wondering what we have been up to. I can assure you that we have been very busy. In addition to working on various tasks, our main focus has been creating the content for the Jury Questioning, which is the topic of today's post.

Before we delve into the specifics, let's recap what the Jury Questioning is all about. The Jury Questioning spans four days, during which you will meet up to five potential jurors each day. The goal is to find jurors who align with your client and increase your chances of achieving the desired verdict. You have the opportunity to question each juror once, gaining insight into their opinions, beliefs, and defining traits.

Each juror possesses a political affiliation (ranging from extreme left to extreme right), a level of education (none, poorly educated, educated, highly educated), wealth (ranging from destitute to wealthy), a religion, and six additional defining traits. In total, a juror can have up to 99 different traits.

The more similar a juror is to your client, the less likely they are to convict. Therefore, having enough "friendly" jurors on the bench significantly increases your chances of winning the case. However, what if there are no similar or sympathetic jurors available? Fear not, because you can also influence the jury's perception through witnesses. The more similarity between a juror and a witness, the more the juror will believe the witness's testimony. So, even if the Jury Pool lacks sympathy for your client, you can still turn the tide by selecting witnesses that resonate with the jurors.

When a juror enters the courtroom, the judge asks them to introduce themselves, sharing their name, age, and place of residence. In their introduction, it’s possible that the juror might drop a hint of one of their six special traits. After that, it's up to you to get to know your potential jurors and uncover their hidden traits. Overall, the Jury Questioning offers 293 questions across 66 topics for you to explore.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39390578/853ff259c488c3885efdd7b0c10f72e3163cf51c.png[/img]
Jurors will answer questions either neutrally or based on their specific traits. The system ensures that their responses are evenly distributed among the jurors, giving you a fair chance to discover them all. However, be aware that jurors may become offended or dislike certain questions. In a Jury Trial, it's up to the juror to decide how long you can question them. If a juror is particularly unresponsive, it may be better to let them go, as a strike-out might leave a negative impression and could harm your case.

To avoid cluttering your desk with sticky notes containing potential and excluded traits, the game provides a handy interface where you can make notes for each juror. These notes will play a key role once the day of questioning concludes. After each day, you will have the opportunity to assess the five jurors you've met and select the ten traits you believe each juror carries. If you identify enough traits correctly, you will gain an overall opinion bonus applied to all jurors at the end of the Jury Selection process.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39390578/a9ec0bf8aa0e8e3926b46068d29bf06f943c316a.png[/img]
Writing trait-specific answers for 99 different traits has been both challenging and rewarding. It has been fascinating to explore questions from so many different angles. Just to give you an idea, it takes approximately 8 hours to come up with 500 answers, including research and spell-checking. Currently, the game includes 1,723 neutral and 23,214 trait-specific answers. We remain committed to adding more throughout the development process because the more answers and perspectives we include, the more interesting and challenging the Jury Questioning will become. We also plan to give the community the chance to propose new topics, questions, and answers once you've all had the opportunity to test the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39390578/084f4355db977a97e50b7190afd81e62dfd89c2b.png[/img]
So, that's the basic rundown of how the Jury Questioning works. Now, you might be wondering what's next for Jury Trial. The work never truly stops, and since we've invested a significant amount of time into the Jury Questioning, there are a few loose ends we still need to tie up. Once those tasks are completed, our focus will shift to creating a demo case for you to play and provide us with much-needed feedback. Rest assured that even if you don't make it into the closed testing phase, the demo case will be released on the store page for everyone to enjoy! We'll share more details about the entire process in a future post, so stay tuned for that.

As always, we're delighted to answer any questions you may have. Feel free to head over to the Community Section, leave a reply below, or chat with us on [url=https://discord.com/invite/bQNesxtakY]Discord[/url].

Thank you so much for your ongoing support.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39390578/4e49a56d89604c53cbc6b035af1e3ac7e769d269.png[/img]

notes.title: Development update & well wishes!
notes.notes:
Greetings Counselors,

Today we would like to give you a quick update on what we have been up to since our last post but most of all wish you a happy new year, especially success, happiness and health in 2023!

Over the past year Jury Trial has grown so much that we’re nearly feature complete. Beside working on sound and Steam integration, we’ll now enter a phase of polishing and adding additional motions, event chains and other items to enrich the cases. Our workload will shift from mechanics and systems to content production.

As you might know, we’ve orientated the development process along the flow of the game. We’ve started with the prerequisites followed by the Pre-Trial and Trial Phase. At the end of our last post, we announced the beginning of the verdict phase which is about to be completed. If you missed the last updates or like to revisit them, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1389140/view/3193622590947091194]here’s[/url] and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1389140/view/3350136629852238243]here’s[/url] the link.

Just like last time, we can’t explain every mechanic and system in detail without going beyond the scope of this post. We’ll do that in due time but if you have questions, feel free to leave a reply on this post, use the Steam boards or have a chat with us over on [url=https://discord.com/invite/bQNesxtakY]discord[/url]. So without further ado, here are the highlights of what has been added to the game and is fully utilizable in the Case Editor:

[list]
[*] dismiss the judge from the case and create an alternative
[*] create fully customizable opening and closing statements for the player and NPC opponent
[*] the date for the closing arguments is determined dynamically in case the trial is prolonged / delayed
[*]added the “written argument” (before the Jury goes into deliberation the player hands in a written argument. In this document scene the player creates arguments by choosing a law / tactic and facts of the case. If the arguments line up with the solution of the case creator, the player gains some bonus points with the jurors)
[*] create pro and contra conviction arguments and tactics including compulsory and supporting arguments. The arguments will be shown on the legal option tab to guide the player and give him possible routes for the case
[*]create fully customizable (multiple) indictments including the possibility to put them into a sequence (e.g. murder, voluntary manslaughter, involuntary manslaughter. The jurors will cast their vote according to the sequence until they reach a guilty verdict or until the defendant was declared not guilty on all counts)
[*]determine the necessary guilty votes for each indictment (unanimous, three-quarter, majority and quorum (case creator decides how many guilty votes it takes to convict))
[*]created a link between dialogue and indictments. It’s now possible to put points on answers that modify the jurors opinion for a certain indictment
[*]created a link between events and indictments. It’s now possible to manipulate the opinions of the jurors through events (all jurors flat, specific groups (e.g. an age group / jurors of a specific political belief etc.) or a specific juror))
[*]introduced a matching value between all protagonists (the matching value determines the opinion of a person to another person by matching all traits (e.g. rich vs poor, political left vs political right) and creates a value. This value is used in different ways e.g. the initial value for each indictment (matching value between defendant and each juror. The similar both persons are the lower is the chance of conviction))
[*]introduced a credibility mechanic for witnesses and experts (matching value between witness vs each juror)
[*]created seven different types of additional traits that manipulate the opinion of the jurors in three categories : chance to convict points, gained through dialogue & credibility
[*]implemented the election of the foreperson. Both player and NPC opponent nominate a juror as foreperson. The other jurors cast their vote along the matching value
[*]implemented the verdict roll (chance to convict = matching value juror vs defendant modified by traits, events and dialogue). In case of a tie (6-6 in a “majority indictment”) the vote of the foreperson decides the outcome
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39390578/5d4f6b87d79aa5a235a2eb3de0aed2e647f1132c.png[/img]

We hope that this overview gives you an idea of what Jury Trial is going to offer. We couldn’t put every change or last detail into the list. But as we’ve said before, if you have any questions do not hesitate to ask, we’re always glad to be of assistance. 

Last but not least, we’d like to thank you for your support, questions and encouragement over the last year. It really helps us to tackle this tremendous project and we hope that you will continue to do so. Thank you.


Cheers to 2023!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39390578/4e49a56d89604c53cbc6b035af1e3ac7e769d269.png[/img]
